text: We evaluated a learned noisy-channel model of weak-label errors refined by expectation-maximization on the BoolQ testbed, measuring performance gap recovered (PGR) across num_seeds = 10 random seeds. The method attains a mean PGR of 0.62 with a standard error of 0.11. Interpreted directly, this indicates that roughly six-tenths of the gap between the weak supervisor and the strong ceiling is recovered on average, though the standard error of 0.11 implies meaningful seed-to-seed spread, so the underlying value could plausibly sit appreciably above or below the point estimate. An important caveat is that no baseline PGR was supplied for this configuration, so we cannot characterize this number as an improvement over, or a regression from, any alternative treatment of weak-label noise; the result stands only as an absolute measurement for this method and testbed. Comparison against a matched naive-finetuning baseline, and extension beyond BoolQ, would be needed before drawing broader conclusions about the channel-plus-EM approach.
